WITH due AS ( SELECT id FROM asset_upload_sessions WHERE org_id = public.auth_active_org_id() AND ( status IN ('created', 'uploading') OR ( status = 'aborted' AND id IN ( SELECT session_id FROM asset_quota_reservations WHERE org_id = public.auth_active_org_id() AND state = 'reserved' ) ) ) AND expires_at <= $1::timestamptz ), expired AS ( UPDATE asset_upload_sessions AS session SET status = 'expired', updated_at = now() FROM due WHERE session.id = due.id RETURNING session.id, session.asset_id, session.expires_at ), staged AS ( /* Mark the reclaim and hand the session's reserved bytes to the staged object in one statement, so an object that physically exists is never momentarily unaccounted and cannot let a concurrent upload oversubscribe. The transfer is guarded on bytes IS NULL so a settled object is never charged twice. */ UPDATE asset_objects AS object SET status = 'deleting', -- Every grant this session issued was clamped to its expires_at, -- so an expired session has no surviving writer; the existing -- hold is kept as the bound for objects whose recorded deadline -- (or conservative migrated hold) already covers it. write_hold_until = GREATEST( object.write_hold_until, expired.expires_at, now() ), reserved_bytes = CASE WHEN object.bytes IS NULL THEN COALESCE(object.reserved_bytes, reservation.bytes) ELSE object.reserved_bytes END, updated_at = now() FROM expired JOIN asset_quota_reservations AS reservation ON reservation.session_id = expired.id AND reservation.state = 'reserved' WHERE object.asset_id = expired.asset_id AND object.kind = 'staging' AND object.status IN ('writing', 'ready') ), released AS ( /* Only after the bytes are inventoried above; both run in this single statement so there is no window charged by neither source. */ UPDATE asset_quota_reservations AS reservation SET state = 'released', released_at = now() FROM expired WHERE reservation.session_id = expired.id AND reservation.state = 'reserved' ) UPDATE assets AS asset SET status = 'failed', failure_code = $2, failure_message = $3, failure_retryable = true, failure_at = now(), -- Retention decides the reclaim clock only. The failure itself is -- what the creator sees, so it is recorded even for an Asset a -- saved draft still holds. orphaned_at = CASE WHEN EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM post_attachments WHERE asset_id = asset.id ) THEN NULL ELSE now() END, orphan_delete_after = CASE WHEN EXISTS ( SELECT 1 FROM post_attachments WHERE asset_id = asset.id ) THEN NULL ELSE now() + make_interval(days => $4) END, updated_at = now() FROM expired WHERE asset.id = expired.asset_id AND asset.status IN ('pending_upload', 'uploading')

SELECT o.id, public.auth_active_user_id() AS user_id, COALESCE(u.uploads, 0) AS uploads, COALESCE(resident.resident_bytes, 0) AS storage_bytes, COALESCE(r.reservation_count, 0) AS active_reservations, COALESCE(r.reservation_bytes, 0) AS active_reservation_bytes FROM organizations o LEFT JOIN usage_records u ON u.org_id = o.id AND u.period = $1 LEFT JOIN LATERAL ( -- One inventory rule for every row that is not durably removed. -- Verified originals, renditions and thumbnails charge their real -- bytes; an in-flight write charges the reservation it still holds; -- and a row claimed for deletion keeps charging either way, because its -- bytes survive in the bucket until the external delete completes and -- so survive a period rollover that resets the usage_records counter. -- GREATEST, not a sum: one physical key cannot hold its old and its -- replacement bytes simultaneously, so a row that recorded measured -- output while still holding the planned reservation is charged the -- larger of the two exactly once. SELECT COALESCE( SUM( GREATEST( COALESCE(object.bytes, 0), COALESCE(object.reserved_bytes, 0) ) ), 0 ) AS resident_bytes FROM asset_objects AS object WHERE object.org_id = o.id AND object.status <> 'deleted' ) resident ON TRUE LEFT JOIN LATERAL ( SELECT COUNT(*) AS reservation_count, COALESCE(SUM(bytes), 0) AS reservation_bytes FROM asset_quota_reservations WHERE org_id = o.id AND state = 'reserved' ) r ON TRUE WHERE o.id = public.auth_active_org_id()
